Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process
You are now ready to begin Route 3 of the Procurement Journey.
Any documents you need are listed below
Specific Considerations and Rules for CSS Contracts

content_blocks.text: View PDF
Route 3 is designed for use by a buyer. If this does not apply to you, please contact your Procurement Function or Centre of Expertise.
This route of the Procurement Journey provides guidance for regulated procurements for goods and services at the GPA procurement threshold and above.
Route 3 does not apply to construction (works) or contracts that cover utilities e.g. running tramways. Please refer to the Construction Handbook for guidance.
Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Contract Notice
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Contract Notices must be used to advertise all Route 3 procedures. Exceptions to this include:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: use of the negotiated procedure without prior publication (only available in strictly defined and exceptional circumstances)
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: a defined list of Care and Support Services contracts between £50,000 and the light touch regime theshold
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: The Contract Notice must contain the minimum and specific requirements for your procurement exercise.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Indicative Budget
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: You may choose to:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: indicate the available budget for delivering the service in question;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: specify the outcomes desired
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: invite providers to submit proposals for achieving the outcomes within the resources available.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Stating an indicative budget ensures that bidders' tenders for delivering the service are affordable. This may be appropriate if, for example, a procurement exercise fails and the organisation moves to negotiation with suppliers.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: This is particularly important if there is an expectation that suppliers will submit consortia bids to allow discussions between suppliers to take place.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: With the exception of the scenarios stated in Contract Notice section above, all Contract Notices must be published on Public Contracts Scotland (PCS).
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: PCS is the national advertising portal which provides suppliers with free access to contract opportunities. It guides you:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: through the process of creating a Notice on its website
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: automatically creates a Notice on the Find a Tender Service
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: If using PCS-T or the SPD (Scotland) word document, you must set out the specific requirements and minimum standards for your procurement. These must be relevant and proportionate and included in your Contract Notice . This is not necessary if using the online SPD (Scotland) Module on PCS as the relevant information is contained within this module.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: If Using OJEU/TED:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: If your procurement was advertised before 11 p.m. on 31 December 2020 (or is a call off from a Framework Agreement or a Dynamic Purchasing System that commenced before this date) you will receive a PCS alert after you have submitted the Contract Notice for publication on PCS. You will also receive a separate mail from Tenders Electronic Daily (TED) with your temporary OJEU reference number.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: Once your Notice is published in the OJEU, TED will send you a permanent OJEU publication number. You must retrospectively include your online SPD (Scotland) with this permanent OJEU number if using the PCS Module.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: If Using FTS:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: If your procurement was advertised after 11 p.m. on 31 December 2020 you will receive an FTS email after you have submitted the Contract Notice for publication on PCS.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: Your Contract Notice must contain details of how bidders can access your procurement documentation.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: From the date you publish your Notice you must make your Procurement Documents available:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: on the internet;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: in unrestricted and full direct access form;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: free of charge
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: The Regulations define ‘procurement documents’ very widely. This includes all documents related to the procurement i.e. including technical specifications, terms and conditions and tender documents to be used at subsequent stages
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: In practical terms, it is not always possible to have all documents available at the start of your procurement exercise. Only in an Open Procedure are you required to have the ITT available from the outset. For all other procedures you must provide sufficiently precise information. This will allow bidders to understand the nature and scope of your requirement and decide whether to request to participate.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
Establishing a Timetable for the Procurement Process

content_blocks.text: PCS-T Publication
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Procurement documents must not be published in PCS-T until you have received your publication reference number from FTS.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: The procurement documents should be published in PCS-T on the same day of whichever of the above events occurs first.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Contract Award Readiness Checklist
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Before a buyer awards a contract they should check the following points:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text:
Action	Checked?
Who was involved in the tender award process? Have there been any changes in staff from those involved during the tender evaluation?	
Did any of the tenderers drop out of the process and decide not to proceed with the tender? Consider if an unknown agreement was made.	
Review the list of proposed suppliers/sub-contractors to be used by the successful bidder? Did these organisations also bid directly for the tender exercise? Such circumstances can lead to a pre-determined outcome as it would be irrelevant who was awarded the work. This may identify cartel operating.

content_blocks.text: Using PCS
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: If uploading Procurement Documents to PCS file size restrictions apply. These are:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: 10Mb per document a maximum of 40Mb for the buyer;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: 10Mb per document with a maximum of 30Mb for the Supplier
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: If you are using PCS-T, attachments cannot be added to the Contract Notice on PCS. You must add your documents to PCS-T.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Using PCS-T
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: If you use PCS-T you must provide time limits for the receipt of tenders (bearing in mind statutory minimums).
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Mixed Procurement Exercises
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Mixed procurements that contain any activity within the scope of the Defence and Security Regulations or the Utilities Directive must refer to their relevant legislation. Such procurement exercises do not come under the guidance of the Procurement Journey.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Where a procurement consists of a mix of activities:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: the main subject of the contract needs to be determined. This will establish which procure ment rules apply e.g. a procurement with a goods and a works element, which has the provision of goods as the main subject matter, should be treated as a goods procurement exercise. (It is important to focus on what the main subject is i.e. there could be a contract with more goods supplied, however, the works element may still be the main subject/purpose of the contract or vice versa.) It is important to note that in this case, the value of the relative spend is not the only factor in identifying the main subject
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: partly services (including Care and Support Services and those detailed in Schedule 3 , and partly goods: the main subject of the contract is determined by which of the services or goods has the highest estimated value
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Care and Support Services and those listed in Schedule 3 and partly for other services: the main subject of the contract is determined by which of the services has the highest estimated value.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Quickfire Guide
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Contract Award - Recommendation Report Contents
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: A Recommendation Report should be used to obtain approval (if required) to award a contract. The report should contain reference to the following:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: a summary of the process to date
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: ensure any decisions for supplier disqualification have been fully documented and that the paperwork is available for inspection
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: recommendation of award & request for approval
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Selection Stage evaluation results (if not contained within previous report)
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: technical & commercial evaluation (including any whole life costing) together with details of any clarifications conducted benefits and savings available
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: details of any risks still present and mitigation plans
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Sustainable Procurement Considerations (life-cycle costing, social, economic and environmental)
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Cyber Security Considerations
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: considerations in relation to Community Benefits
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: details on how the tender outcome will meet the requirements identified in the Commodity/Service Strategy.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Once you have obtained approval, you can notify both the successful and unsuccessful tenderers of the outcome and they should be notified as soon as possible.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Information provided to tenderers must, where applicable, include the grounds for any decision:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: not to conclude a Framework Agreement ;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: not to award a contract that has been advertised;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: to recommence the procedure;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: not to implement a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS).
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Consideration must also be given to Planning , Sustainable Procurement and Risk Managemen t throughout this stage of the Procurement Journey.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Route 3 is not intended to replace training and it is assumed that individuals will have been trained in:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: the Procurement Reform (Scotland) Act 2014 and any other legislative requirements;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: the procurement cycle;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: any applicable local procurement policies, guidelines and governance arrangements.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: The main objectives of this route are:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: to provide a step-by-step guide to conducting a procurement exercise for goods and services;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: to provide a set of guides and templates that can be used to collate and analyse the data required when conducting the procurement exercise;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: to standardise the public sector procurement process across organisations;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: to highlight some key legal and policy obligations and considerations that apply throughout the procurement process
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Before beginning Route 3, please consider the following:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: good procurement is not just about buying well but it's often about buying less or, indeed, not buying at all .
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Depe nding on the specifics of your procurement exercise, the types of questions you might ask of stakeholders before starting your procurement could include:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: have alternatives to procuring been considered and ruled out?
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: do you have a budget?
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: is there a robust documented business case supporting this procurement?
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: will this expenditure stand up to public scrutiny?
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: has Procurement been involved in the development of the business case?
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: c an Procurement provide support with cost options; enabling flexibility; minimising risk; and/or to inform decisions regarding the way forward?
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: are you aware of opportunities to buy your specific requirements through existing collaborative contracts? If so, do you know how to access them?
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: can you use output information from the Prioritisation Tool
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: for Care and Support Services, when considering continuing an existing service the Flowchart to Help Decision Making for the Continuation of an Existing Service provides additional guidance;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: for Care and Support Services, please also refer to Specific Considerations and Rules for CSS Contracts .
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Consideration must also be given to Planning , Sustainable Procurement and Risk Management throughout the Journey.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Please note that purchases of goods and services may routinely be the subject of Freedom of Information (FoI) requests.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Please be aware that where the term 'commodity' is used within the Procurement Journey this can equally refer to categories of goods and/or services.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Please note that, other than on the final contract, there is no legal requirement for a "wet" signature at any point of the procurement process, however, please check your individual organisation's policy regarding signatures .
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: You should use Lessons Learned from previous contracts/procurement exercises to inform your new strategy. As you progress through the Journey you should constantly re-inform your strategy with any new information.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: There are natural break points within the Procurement Journey. These can be used as review points for sign off and approval to proceed to the next stage of the process.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Procurement Exercise Review and Approval
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Suggested review and sign off points are:
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: at project initiation;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: after initial Opportunity Assessment;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: for approval of strategy, including budget;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: for contract management approach;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: for approval of Procurement Documents;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: at Contract Award stage;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: at implementation stage;
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Throughout the Journey you will see reference to these sign off points at the relevant sections with supporting documents.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: Any approval and review of the project plan should be subject to your organisation's governance arrangements.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice

content_blocks.text: You are now ready to begin Route 3 of the Procurement Journey.
heading_path: Contract Notice, Procurement Documents and Contract Award Notice
